content: The National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP) is a nonprofit organization headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota. It operates the federally funded registry of volunteer hematopoietic cell donors in the United States. As of October 2007, approximately 8 million individuals have volunteered to donate hematopoietic cells to patients requiring hematopoietic cell transplantation. Since its establishment in 1986, the NMDP has facilitated 30,000 successful transplants by December 3, 2007. The NMDP registry also includes over 69,000 umbilical cord blood units, which serve as an alternative source of hematopoietic cells for transplantation. Hematopoietic cell transplants are utilized to treat a variety of life-threatening conditions, including leukemia, lymphoma, aplastic anemia, certain immune system disorders, and genetic diseases. Hematopoietic cells, which are blood-forming stem cells, can be derived from bone marrow, umbilical cord blood, or peripheral blood stem cells (PBSCs). These cells have the ability to multiply and differentiate into the three main types of blood cells: red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. The NMDP registry is one of many registries worldwide that maintain databases of unrelated donors and cord blood units. Large registries are essential because only about 30% of patients in need of hematopoietic cell transplantation can find a suitable HLA-matched donor within their family. For the remaining 70%, an unrelated donor is required. The probability of two random individuals being HLA-matched is less than 1 in 20,000, necessitating a large pool of volunteer donors for a registry to be effective. The NMDP coordinates hematopoietic cell transplants through a global network of affiliated organizations, primarily hospitals. These organizations collaborate with the NMDP to arrange the collection and transfer of donated bone marrow or cord blood. When an adult volunteer donor registers with the NMDP, their HLA information is entered into the NMDP’s database, along with their contact information, so they can be reached if matched with a patient. The NMDP also lists over 69,000 cord blood units stored at 24 affiliated cord blood banks worldwide (as of October 2007). Physicians can search the NMDP registry on behalf of patients by submitting the patient’s HLA tissue type. The NMDP then searches its database for a matching donor. If a match is found, the NMDP contacts the potential donor, educates them about the donation process, and asks if they are willing to proceed. If the donor agrees, they undergo a medical examination, including infectious disease testing. If they meet all requirements, their bone marrow or PBSCs are collected and transported to the patient via courier. The NMDP is connected internationally through its participation with Bone Marrow Donors Worldwide (BMDW), an organization based in Leiden, The Netherlands, that facilitates communication among global registries. There are an estimated 10 million volunteer hematopoietic cell donors worldwide, and most national registries, including the NMDP, have access to these donors through the BMDW or individual agreements. Although based in the United States, the NMDP has extensive international connections. Over 40% of the transplants arranged by the NMDP involve either a foreign patient or a foreign donor. The NMDP collaborates with seven donor centers outside the United States, located in The Netherlands, Israel, Sweden, Norway, and Germany (three centers). Additionally, the NMDP is affiliated with 17 transplant centers outside the United States where patients can receive transplants using cells from NMDP donors. While the NMDP is the only federally funded and congressionally authorized stem cell registry in the United States, there are three smaller registries. The Caitlin Raymond International Registry, based at the UMass Memorial Medical Center in Massachusetts, has approximately 64,000 adult volunteer donors and access to about 10,000 cord blood units. The American Bone Marrow Donor Registry (ABMDR), based in Mandeville, Louisiana, has about 32,000 adult volunteer donors. The Caitlin Raymond International Registry serves as the search center for the ABMDR. The Gift of Life Bone Marrow Foundation, based in Boca Raton, Florida, was established in 1991 to recruit donors of Jewish ethnic ancestry. It has registered approximately 110,000 volunteer donors and has access to about 400 cord blood units. In May 2004, the Gift of Life Bone Marrow Foundation partnered with the NMDP, becoming an Associate Donor Registry. In July 2007, the Caitlin Raymond International Registry became affiliated with the NMDP. The NMDP receives approximately $23 million annually from the U.S. government through the Health Resources and Services Administration. Additional funding is provided by the U.S. Navy. The program also generates income from donations, fees charged to donors for tissue typing (approximately $50 as of 2006, waived for some minority groups), fees for in-depth database searches (initial searches are free, but full searches can cost several thousand dollars), and fees charged to transplanting hospitals once a match is found and the stem cells are transferred. The latter fee is about $21,000, which is slightly higher than fees charged by other U.S. and international registries. The total cost of a completed transplant to the patient or their insurance company can range from $100,000 to $250,000. The NMDP compensates affiliated donor centers and recruitment groups for every new donor they register.
